summary: A large amount of slime or honey blocks will crash the game
description: If you place many slime blocks or honey blocks (more than 4000). If you render them it will crash the game completely and you can t join the world anymore.
Steps to Reproduce:
1. Launch Minecraft.
2. Create a new Creative world with default settings.
3. Place more than 4000 slime blocks or honey blocks in the world.
4. Wait until the blocks are rendered.
5. Observe that the game crashes completely, preventing you from joining the world again.
Observed Behavior:
When a player places more than 4,000 slime blocks or honey blocks in a single world, attempting to render or load these blocks causes the game to crash completely. This crash results in the player being unable to rejoin the world, as the game fails to load the chunk containing the excessive number of blocks. The issue appears to be related to the game's rendering engine and its ability to handle large quantities of block entities simultaneously. 

Upon crashing, the game may display an error message indicating a failure to allocate memory or render the blocks, leading to a complete shutdown of the application. This issue can be reproduced consistently by exceeding the specified block limit, and it is not resolved by removing blocks or restarting the game. The only solution is to access the world file directly and remove the offending blocks using external tools, or to restore the world from a backup prior to the block placement. 

This bug is critical as it affects world accessibility and player experience, particularly in creative builds or large-scale projects where many blocks are used.
Expected Behavior: When placing a large number of slime or honey blocks (more than 4000), the game should handle the rendering of these blocks without crashing. Players should be able to join the world and interact with the blocks normally, regardless of the quantity placed. The game should maintain stability and performance, allowing for smooth gameplay even with high block counts in the environment.
